newsitem.title: USA: Centennial to restate results, sees losses.
newsitem.headline: Centennial to restate results, sees losses.

text.p: Centennial Technologies Inc said Tuesday it expects to restate its financial results for fiscal 1996, ended June 30, 1996, and the first quarter of fiscal 1997, and expects to report losses for both periods.
It also said it would revise its fiscal 1997 second quarter results and would have a loss for that period as well.
The restatement is based on preliminary results of a special review and is expected to be material, the company said.
To date, the special review has focused primarily on year-end 1996 and 1997, Centennial said.
"Certain financial records of the company appear to have been falsified and may affect the ability to determine the accuracy of financial statements," it said.

Centennial's lender has informed the company that it is in default of covenants regarding its revolving credit line. The lender has indicated any further loans will be made at the lender's discretion, Centennial said.
If financing does not become available, the company might not have sufficient liquidity to meet its cash needs, it said.

The company said it is aware that up to 14 lawsuits have been filed against it on behalf of purchasers of Centennial securities during varying time periods, including August 21, 1996, through February 11, 1997.
Also, the Securities and Exchange Commission has indicated it is investigating the company, Centennial said.

Last week the company said it had fired its chief executive officer, Emanual Pinez, and removed its chief financial officer, James Murphy, and was looking into the accuracy of its recent financial reports.
Centennial shares closed at 16-3/8 on February 10 and have not traded since then.
